    Research

    Research

    Applied ML for perception and imaging

    My research work centers on sensor fusion, 3D detection, segmentation, and diffusion-based modeling for computer vision systems.

    Kim's Lab

    University of Michigan

    May 2023 - Dec 2025

    Advisor: Dr. Hun-Seok Kim Office: 2238 EECS, 1301 Beal Avenue
    • Built a temporal sensor fusion pipeline using a transformer backbone for nuScenes LiDAR and camera inputs.
    • Designed experiments for 3D object detection training under known and unknown parameter settings.
    • Improved latent diffusion sampling for inverse imaging and reported an FID score of 37.2.
    • Applied latent diffusion to a source-channel decoding setup and achieved 24.4 dB reconstruction PSNR.
    Sensor fusion 3D detection Diffusion nuScenes

    Other labs

    Computer vision and medical imaging

    Burris Lab

    PLRI Lab

    Built semantic segmentation tooling for sclera regions, partial annotation workflows, and training utilities.

    Dr. Shyam's Lab
